threads.title: The Sutra of Selfless Action
threads.note: From the right to action without its fruit, through unattached work offered to Brahman, to natural duty — and finally to surrender beyond all duties.

threads.title: The Sutra of the Undying Self
threads.note: From 'never was there a time when I did not exist' to the Lord seated in every heart.

threads.title: The Sutra of Equanimity
threads.note: Evenness of mind as yoga, matured into the steady sage, the beloved devotee, the one beyond the guṇas — and the serenity that leads to supreme devotion.

threads.title: The Sutra of Devotion
threads.note: From the dear jñānī-devotee to 'fix your mind on me' — sealed by the call to take refuge.

threads.title: The Sutra of Surrender
threads.note: Arjuna's first surrender as disciple deepens into the final 'take refuge in me alone'.

threads.title: The Sutra of Divine Protection
threads.note: The avatāra who comes age after age; the promise that 'my devotee never perishes'.

threads.title: The Sutra of the Mind
threads.note: From the senses that carry away the mind to the discipline of practice and dispassion and the solitary meditator of Chapter 18.

threads.title: The Sutra of Knowledge
threads.note: Knowledge as the highest sacrifice and purifier, maturing into 'Vāsudeva is all' and knowing him in truth.

threads.title: The Sutra of One's Own Path
threads.note: The warrior's duty widened into the universal principle of one's own dharma.

threads.title: The Sutra of Faith
threads.note: Faith that leads to knowledge and peace, shaped by one's nature, and that liberates the listener.

threads.title: The Sutra of the Three Qualities
threads.note: From 'the guṇas act' to the guṇas binding the Self and shaping faith, food, sacrifice and happiness.

threads.title: The Sutra of Sacrifice
threads.note: Work as yajña, the cosmic wheel of sacrifice, Brahman-as-offering, and 'whatever you do, offer it to me'.

threads.title: The Sutra of the Final Hour
threads.note: Whatever one remembers at death, to that one goes — so 'remember me always and fight'.

threads.title: The Sutra of the Cosmic Vision
threads.note: From the Self in every heart and the spark of glory, to a thousand suns, Time the destroyer, and the vision granted only to devotion.

dialogues.question: How can I fight my own kin? Victory, kingdom, pleasure — what are they worth?
dialogues.theme: The immortality of the Self dissolves grief.

dialogues.question: My nature is overcome by pity; my mind is confused about dharma — tell me decisively what is good.
dialogues.theme: The disciple's surrender opens the teaching.

dialogues.question: What are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady? How do they speak, sit and walk?
dialogues.theme: Portrait of the person of steady wisdom.

dialogues.question: If knowledge is superior to action, why urge me to this terrible deed?
dialogues.theme: Two paths, one goal: no one can remain actionless.

dialogues.question: By what is a person impelled to sin, even unwillingly, as if by force?
dialogues.theme: Desire and anger, born of rajas, are the enemy.

dialogues.question: Your birth is recent, Vivasvān's ancient — how could you have taught him in the beginning?
dialogues.theme: The doctrine of divine descent (avatāra).

dialogues.question: You praise renunciation of action and also its yoga — tell me which one is better.
dialogues.theme: Karma-yoga is superior; both lead to the same goal.

dialogues.question: The mind is restless, turbulent and obstinate — as hard to control as the wind.
dialogues.theme: Practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion (vairāgya).

dialogues.question: What becomes of one with faith whose mind strays from yoga — do they perish like a broken cloud?
dialogues.theme: No doer of good ever comes to grief.

dialogues.question: What is Brahman? What is adhyātma, karma, adhibhūta, adhidaiva, adhiyajña — and how are you known at death?
dialogues.theme: Remembrance at the hour of death.

dialogues.question: Tell me fully your divine glories — in what forms should I contemplate you?
dialogues.theme: The divine manifest in the excellent of every kind.

dialogues.question: I wish to see your Īśvara form, O Supreme Person — if you think I am able.
dialogues.theme: The gift of divine sight.

dialogues.question: Tell me who you are, so terrible in form — I do not understand your purpose.
dialogues.theme: 'I am Time, destroyer of worlds' — be merely the instrument.

dialogues.question: Overjoyed yet shaken with fear — show me again your gentle four-armed form.
dialogues.theme: Only by undivided devotion can I be seen thus.

dialogues.question: Who are better versed in yoga — devotees of your form, or those who worship the imperishable unmanifest?
dialogues.theme: Both reach me; the path of devotion is easier for the embodied.

dialogues.question: I wish to know prakṛti and puruṣa, the field and its knower, knowledge and its object.
dialogues.theme: The body is the field; the Self, its knower.

dialogues.question: By what marks is one known who has gone beyond the three guṇas? How do they transcend them?
dialogues.theme: Equality in all dualities; unswerving devotion.

dialogues.question: What is the standing of those who worship with faith but set aside scriptural injunctions?
dialogues.theme: Faith takes the shape of one's guṇa.

dialogues.question: I wish to know the essence of saṃnyāsa and of tyāga, and the difference between them.
dialogues.theme: Renounce the fruit, not the duty.

dialogues.question: Have you heard this with a one-pointed mind? Is your delusion born of ignorance destroyed?
dialogues.theme: 'My delusion is gone, my memory regained… I shall do your word.'

chains.title: The Ladder of Fall
chains.summary: Brooding on sense-objects breeds attachment; attachment, desire; desire, anger; anger, bewilderment; bewilderment, loss of memory; loss of memory, the ruin of reason — and with reason lost, one perishes.

chains.title: The Ladder of Ascent
chains.summary: Moving among objects with senses under control, free of attachment and aversion, one attains serenity; in serenity sorrows end; without peace, how can there be happiness?

chains.title: Desire and Anger, Born of Rajas
chains.summary: It is desire, it is anger, born of the guṇa of rajas — all-devouring, the enemy here.

chains.title: The Threefold Gate of Ruin
chains.summary: Desire, anger and greed — the threefold gate of hell that destroys the self. Freed from these three, one walks the highest path.

chains.title: What Each Guṇa Yields
chains.summary: From sattva arises knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, heedlessness, delusion and ignorance.

chains.title: From Faith to Peace
chains.summary: The one with faith, devoted and master of the senses, attains knowledge; having attained it, soon reaches supreme peace.

chains.title: The Doubting Soul
chains.summary: The ignorant, the faithless and the doubting soul perish; for the doubter there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.

chains.title: The Ladder of Practice
chains.summary: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation better than knowledge; renouncing the fruits of action better than meditation — and from renunciation, peace follows at once.

chains.title: Arjuna's Collapse
chains.summary: Attachment to kin clouds Arjuna's judgment of dharma; confusion sinks into despair, and despair into the faint-heartedness Krishna rebukes in 2.3.

chains.title: Ascent to Supreme Devotion
chains.summary: Abandoning ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, one becomes fit for Brahman; serene, neither grieving nor craving, equal to all beings, one attains supreme devotion.

nodes.title: Arjuna Visada Yoga
nodes.summary: The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita - "Arjuna Vishada Yoga" introduces the setup, the setting, the characters and the circumstances that led to the epic battle of Mahabharata, fought between the Pandavas and the Kauravas. It outlines the reasons that led to the revelation of the of Bhagavad Gita.

nodes.title: Sankhya Yoga

nodes.name: विभूतियोग
nodes.title: Vibhooti Yoga
nodes.meaning: Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God
nodes.summary: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vibhooti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals Himself as the cause of all causes. He describes His various manifestations and opulences in order to increase Arjuna's Bhakti. Arjuna is fully convinced of Lord's paramount position and proclaims him to be the Supreme Personality. He prays to Krishna to describe more of His divine glories which are like nectar to hear.

nodes.meaning: Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God
nodes.summary: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga". In this chapter, Arjuna requests Krishna to reveal His Universal Cosmic Form that encompasses all the universes, the entire existence. Arjuna is granted divine vision to be able to see the entirety of creation in the body of the Supreme Lord Krishna.

nodes.name: भक्तियोग
nodes.title: Bhakti Yoga
nodes.summary: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Bhakti Yoga". nodes.label: Sri Krishna
nodes.role: The Divine Teacher, charioteer of Arjuna
nodes.desc: Speaker of the Gita — 'Śrī Bhagavān' — revealed as the Supreme Person (15.18) and as the cosmic form (Ch. 11).

nodes.label: Arjuna
nodes.desc: Third Pandava, the archer of the Gāṇḍīva. His collapse (Ch. 1) and questions frame the whole dialogue; his last words are 'my delusion is gone' (18.73).

nodes.label: Sanjaya
nodes.role: The Narrator, seer by Vyasa's grace
nodes.desc: Dhritarashtra's charioteer, granted divine sight by Vyasa to narrate the battle; he closes the Gita in rapture (18.74–78).

nodes.label: Dhritarashtra
nodes.desc: The blind Kuru king whose single question — 'what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?' (1.1) — opens the Gita.

nodes.label: Duryodhana
nodes.desc: Eldest son of Dhritarashtra. Surveying the armies, he addresses Drona with anxious bravado (1.3–11).

nodes.label: Bhishma
nodes.desc: The grand old man of the Kurus, bound by his vow; his lion-roar and conch begin the battle (1.12).

nodes.label: Dronacharya
nodes.desc: Arjuna's own teacher in arms, now on the opposing side — whom Arjuna asks how he can strike (2.4).

nodes.label: Karna
nodes.role: Kaurava champion, son of the charioteer
nodes.desc: The great archer, unknowingly Arjuna's elder brother; seen entering the cosmic mouths in 11.26.

nodes.label: Bhima
nodes.desc: The mighty Vṛkodara, who blows the great conch Pauṇḍra (1.15).

nodes.label: Yudhishthira
nodes.desc: Son of Kunti, who blows the conch Anantavijaya (1.16).

nodes.label: Ved Vyasa
nodes.desc: The sage-poet by whose grace Sanjaya heard this supreme yoga (18.75); Krishna names himself 'Vyāsa among sages' (10.37).

nodes.label: Vivasvan (Sun)
nodes.desc: 'I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvān; Vivasvān told it to Manu; Manu to Ikṣvāku' (4.1) — the lineage of the teaching.

nodes.label: Manu
nodes.desc: Second link in the lineage of the yoga (4.1); the Manus are born of Krishna's mind (10.6).

nodes.label: Ikshvaku
nodes.role: First king of the Solar dynasty
nodes.desc: Third link in the lineage — 'thus handed down in succession, the royal sages knew it' (4.1–2).

nodes.label: Drupada & Dhrishtadyumna
nodes.role: Panchala king and his son, the Pandava commander
nodes.desc: Duryodhana points out 'the son of Drupada, your wise disciple' who arrayed the Pandava host (1.3).

nodes.label: Abhimanyu (Saubhadra)
nodes.desc: The mighty-armed son of Subhadra who blows his conch with the Pandava heroes (1.6, 1.18).

nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च
nodes.snippet: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures stand here in battle, having renounced life and wealth.

nodes.label: BG 1.34
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives—

nodes.label: BG 1.35
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: These I do not wish to kill, O Krishna, even though they kill me, for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; leave alone killing them for the sake of the earth."

nodes.label: BG 1.36
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure could be ours, O Janardana? Only sin would accrue to us from killing these felons.

nodes.label: BG 1.37
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our relatives; for how can we be happy by killing our own kin, O Madhava (Krishna)?

nodes.label: BG 1.38
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Though they, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see no evil in the destruction of families and no sin in hostility to friends,

nodes.label: BG 1.39
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Why should we not, who clearly see the evil in the destruction of families, learn to turn away from this sin, O Janardana (Krishna)?

nodes.label: BG 1.40
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: In the destruction of a family, the immemorial religious rites of that family perish; on the destruction of spirituality, impiety indeed, overwhelms the whole family.

nodes.label: BG 1.41
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: O Krishna, by the prevalence of impiety, the women of the family become corrupt; and, when women are corrupted, O Varshenya (descendant of Vrishni), intermingling of castes arises.

nodes.label: BG 1.42
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Confusion of castes leads to hell for the slayers of the family, for their forebears fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and libations of water.

nodes.label: BG 1.43
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: By these evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, which cause confusion of castes, the eternal religious rites of the caste and the family are destroyed.

nodes.label: BG 1.44
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: We have heard, O Janardana, that those men in whose families the religious practices have been destroyed are inevitably destined to dwell in hell for an unknown period.

nodes.label: BG 1.45
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्
nodes.snippet: Alas! We are involved in a great sin, for we are prepared to kill our kinsmen, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.

nodes.label: BG 1.46
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, should slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.

nodes.label: BG 1.47
nodes.speaker: sanjaya
nodes.snippet: Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken in the midst of the battlefield, Arjuna cast away his bow and arrow and, his mind overwhelmed with sorrow, sat down on the seat of the chariot.

nodes.label: BG 2.1
nodes.speaker: sanjaya
nodes.snippet: Sanjaya said: To him, who was thus overcome with pity, despondent, with eyes full of tears and agitated, Madhusudana (the destroyer of Madhu) or Krishna spoke these words.

nodes.label: BG 2.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "From whence has this perilous strait come upon you, this dejection which is unworthy of you, disgraceful, and which will close the gates of heaven upon…

nodes.label: BG 2.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते
nodes.snippet: Do not yield to impotence, O Arjuna, son of Pritha. It does not befit you. Cast off this mean weakness of the heart! Stand up, O conqueror of foes!

nodes.label: BG 2.4
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "O Madhusudana, how can I fight in battle with arrows against Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of being worshipped, O destroyer of enemies?"

nodes.label: BG 2.5
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Better it is, indeed, in this world to accept alms than to slay the most noble teachers. But if I were to kill them, even in this world, all my enjoyments of wealth and…

nodes.label: BG 2.6
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: I can hardly tell which would be better, that we should conquer them or that they should conquer us. Even the sons of Dhritarashtra, whom we do not wish to slay, stand facing us.

nodes.label: BG 2.7
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: My heart is overpowered by the taint of pity; my mind is confused as to my duty. I ask Thee: Tell me decisively what is good for me. I am Thy disciple; instruct me, who has…

nodes.label: BG 2.8
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: I do not see that this sorrow that burns up my senses would be removed, even if I were to attain prosperous and unrivaled dominion on earth or lordship over the gods.

nodes.label: BG 2.9
nodes.speaker: sanjaya
nodes.snippet: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, the Lord of the senses, Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and destroyer of foes, said, "I will not fight," and became silent.

nodes.label: BG 2.10
nodes.speaker: sanjaya
nodes.snippet: To him who was despondent in the midst of the two armies, Krishna, smiling, O Bharata, spoke these words.

nodes.label: BG 2.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for; yet, you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead."

nodes.label: BG 2.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः
nodes.snippet: Nor, at any time, was I not, nor thou, nor these rulers of men; nor, verily, shall we ever cease to be hereafter.

nodes.label: BG 2.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Just as the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too does it pass into another body; the steadfast one does not grieve over this.

nodes.label: BG 2.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The contact of the senses with the objects, O son of Kunti, which causes heat and cold, pleasure and pain, has a beginning and an end; they are impermanent; endure them…

nodes.label: BG 2.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ
nodes.snippet: That firm man, whom surely these afflictions do not, O chief among men, to whom pleasure and pain are the same, is fit for attaining immortality.

nodes.label: BG 2.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः
nodes.snippet: The unreal has no being; there is no non-being of the real; the truth about both has been seen by the knowers of the truth (or the seers of the essence).

nodes.label: BG 2.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्
nodes.snippet: Know that to be indestructible, by which all this is pervaded. No one can cause the destruction of that, the Imperishable.

nodes.label: BG 2.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: These bodies of the embodied Self, which are eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable, are said to have an end. Therefore, fight, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 2.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्
nodes.snippet: He who takes the Self to be the slayer and he who thinks it is slain, neither of them knows. It does not slay, nor is it slain.

nodes.label: BG 2.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: It is not born, nor does it ever die; after having been, it again does not cease to be; unborn, eternal, changeless, and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.

nodes.label: BG 2.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Whoever knows it to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and inexhaustible, how can that person slay, O Arjuna, or cause to be slain?

nodes.label: BG 2.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so too the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.

nodes.label: BG 2.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः
nodes.snippet: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, wind cannot dry it.

nodes.label: BG 2.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, nor dried up; it is eternal, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, and ancient.

nodes.label: BG 2.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: This Self is said to be unmanifested, unthinkable, and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing this to be so, you should not grieve.

nodes.label: BG 2.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्
nodes.snippet: But even if thou thinkest of It as constantly being born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed one, thou shouldst not grieve.

nodes.label: BG 2.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च
nodes.snippet: For the born, death is certain, and for the dead, birth is certain; therefore, you should not grieve over the inevitable.

nodes.label: BG 2.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their middle state, O Arjuna, and unmanifest again in their end. What is there to grieve about?

nodes.label: BG 2.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: One sees this (the Self) as a wonder; another speaks of it as a wonder; another hears of it as a wonder; yet, having heard, none understands it at all.

nodes.label: BG 2.30
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: This indweller in the body of everyone is ever indestructible, O Arjuna; therefore, you should not grieve for any creature.

nodes.label: BG 2.31
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Further, having regard to your duty, you should not waver, for there is nothing higher for a Kshatriya than a righteous war.

nodes.label: BG 2.32
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna! who are called to fight in such a battle that comes of its own accord as an open door to heaven.

nodes.label: BG 2.33
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि
nodes.snippet: But if you will not fight this righteous war, then having abandoned your own duty and reputation, you will incur sin.

nodes.label: BG 2.34
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: People will also recount your everlasting dishonor; and for one who has been honored, dishonor is worse than death.

nodes.label: BG 2.35
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The great chariot-warriors will think that you have withdrawn from the battle out of fear, and you will be held in low esteem by those who have held you in high regard.

nodes.label: BG 2.36
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Your enemies, scoffing at your power, will speak many abusive words—what could be more painful than this?

nodes.label: BG 2.37
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्
nodes.snippet: Slain, you will obtain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth; therefore, stand up, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight.

nodes.label: BG 2.38
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat equal, engage in battle for the sake of battle; thus, you shall not incur sin.

nodes.label: BG 2.39
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु
nodes.snippet: This, which has been taught to you, is wisdom concerning Sankhya. Now listen to wisdom concerning Yoga, endowed with which, O Arjuna, you shall cast off the bonds of action.

nodes.label: BG 2.40
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: In this, there is no loss of effort, nor is there any harm produced, nor any transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects one from great fear.

nodes.label: BG 2.41
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Here, O joy of the Kurus, there is only one single-pointed determination; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the indecisive.

nodes.label: BG 2.42
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The unwise, taking pleasure in the eulogizing words of the Vedas, utter flowery speech, saying, "There is nothing else," O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 2.43
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Full of desires, with heaven as their goal, (they speak words that are directed to ends) leading to new births as the result of their works, and prescribe various methods…

nodes.label: BG 2.44
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: For those who are attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are drawn away by such teachings, their determinate reason is not formed which is steadily bent on meditation and…

nodes.label: BG 2.45
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes. O Arjuna, free yourself from the pairs of opposites and ever remain in the quality of Sattva,…

nodes.label: BG 2.46
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: To the Brahmana who has known the Self, all the Vedas are of as much use as a reservoir of water would be in a place where there is a flood.

nodes.label: BG 2.47
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Your right is only to work, but not to its results; do not let the results of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.

nodes.label: BG 2.48
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय
nodes.snippet: Perform action, O Arjuna, being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and balanced in success and failure; evenness of mind is called Yoga.

nodes.label: BG 2.49
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Far lower than the Yoga of wisdom is action, O Arjuna. Seek thou refuge in wisdom; wretched are those whose motive is the fruit.

nodes.label: BG 2.50
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Endowed with wisdom and evenness of mind, one casts off in this life both good and evil deeds; therefore, devote yourself to Yoga; Yoga is skill in action.

nodes.label: BG 2.51
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः
nodes.snippet: The wise, possessing knowledge, having abandoned the fruits of their actions, and being freed from the bonds of birth, go to the place which is beyond all evil.

nodes.label: BG 2.52
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When your intellect passes beyond the mire of delusion, then you will attain indifference to what has been heard and what has yet to be heard.

nodes.label: BG 2.53
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When your intellect, which is perplexed by the Vedic texts you have read, stands immovable and steady in the Self, then you will attain Self-realization.

nodes.label: BG 2.54
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, what is the description of one who has steady wisdom and is merged in the superconscious state? How does one of steady wisdom speak, how do they sit,…

nodes.label: BG 2.55
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "When a man completely casts off, O Arjuna, all the desires of the mind and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then he is said to be one of steady…

nodes.label: BG 2.56
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He whose mind is not shaken by adversity, who does not long for pleasures, and is free from attachment, fear, and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.

nodes.label: BG 2.57
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who is everywhere without attachment, upon encountering anything good or bad, neither rejoices nor hastens; his wisdom is firm.

nodes.label: BG 2.58
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When, like the tortoise which withdraws all its limbs on all sides, he withdraws his senses from the sense-objects, then his wisdom becomes steady.

nodes.label: BG 2.59
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The objects of the senses turn away from the abstinent man, leaving the longing behind; but his longing also turns away upon seeing the Supreme.

nodes.label: BG 2.60
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, can violently carry away the mind of a wise person, even though they are striving to control them.

nodes.label: BG 2.61
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः
nodes.snippet: Having restrained them all, he should sit steadfast, intent on Me; his wisdom is steady whose senses are under control.

nodes.label: BG 2.62
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When one thinks of objects, attachment to them arises; from attachment, desire is born; from desire, anger arises.

nodes.label: BG 2.63
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Anger leads to delusion, which causes loss of memory; this, in turn, leads to the destruction of discrimination, resulting in destruction.

nodes.label: BG 2.64
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But the self-controlled man, moving among objects with the senses restrained and free from attraction and repulsion, attains peace.

nodes.label: BG 2.65
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: In that peace, all pains are destroyed; for the intellect of the tranquil-minded soon becomes steady.

nodes.label: BG 2.66
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: There is no knowledge of the Self for the unsteady, and no meditation is possible for the unsteady, and no peace for the unmeditative, and how can there be happiness for one…

nodes.label: BG 2.67
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: For the mind, which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, carries away his discrimination, as the wind carries away a boat on the waters.

nodes.label: BG 2.68
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, O mighty-armed Arjuna, his knowledge is steady whose senses are completely restrained from sense objects.

nodes.label: BG 2.69
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी
nodes.snippet: That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man is awake; when all beings are awake, that is night for the sage who sees.

nodes.label: BG 2.70
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He attains peace into whom all desires enter, just as waters enter the ocean which, filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the man who is full of desires.

nodes.label: BG 2.71
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: That person attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves about without longing, without the sense of ownership, and without egoism.

nodes.label: BG 2.72
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति
nodes.snippet: O son of Pritha, this is the eternal state, the Brahmic seat. Attaining this, one is not deluded. Being established in it, one attains oneness with Brahman even at the end of life.

nodes.label: BG 3.1
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said: If Thou thinkest that knowledge is superior to action, O Krishna, why then, O Kesava, doest Thou ask me to engage in this terrible action?

nodes.label: BG 3.2
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: With this seemingly perplexing speech, you seem to be confusing my understanding; therefore, tell me one certain way by which I may attain bliss.

nodes.label: BG 3.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "In this world, there is a twofold path, as I said before, O sinless one: the path of knowledge of the Sankhyas and the path of action of the Yogins."

nodes.label: BG 3.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Man does not reach actionlessness by not performing actions; nor does he attain perfection by mere renunciation.

nodes.label: BG 3.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Verily, no one can remain for even a moment without performing action; for everyone is made to act helplessly, indeed, by the qualities born of Nature.

nodes.label: BG 3.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्
nodes.snippet: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking of the sense-objects in his mind, he of deluded understanding is called a hypocrite.

nodes.label: BG 3.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But whoever, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, engages himself in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, he excels.

nodes.label: BG 3.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः
nodes.snippet: Perform your bounden duty, for action is superior to inaction, and even the maintenance of the body would not be possible for you through inaction.

nodes.label: BG 3.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The world is bound by actions other than those performed for the sake of sacrifice; do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), perform actions for that sake alone, free from…

nodes.label: BG 3.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Creator, having in the beginning created mankind together with sacrifice, said, "By this shall you propagate; let this be the milch cow of your desires—the cow that yields…

nodes.label: BG 3.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: With this, nourish the gods, and may the gods nourish you; thus, nourishing each other, you shall attain the highest good.

nodes.label: BG 3.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will give you the desired objects. So, he who enjoys the objects given by the gods without offering anything in return is indeed a thief.

nodes.label: BG 3.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The righteous who eat the remnants of the sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those sinful ones who cook food solely for their own sake indeed consume sin.

nodes.label: BG 3.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: From food come forth beings; from rain, food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain, and sacrifice is born of action.

nodes.label: BG 3.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Know that action comes from Brahma, and Brahma comes from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervasive Brahma ever rests in sacrifice.

nodes.label: BG 3.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion, who is of sinful life, rejoicing in the senses, lives in vain, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 3.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But for that man who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self and is content in the Self alone, indeed there is nothing to do.

nodes.label: BG 3.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: For him, there is no interest whatsoever in what is done or not done; nor does he depend on any being for any purpose.

nodes.label: BG 3.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the actions that should be done; for by performing actions without attachment, one reaches the Supreme.

nodes.label: BG 3.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Janaka and others attained perfection indeed through action alone; even with the intention of protecting the masses, you should perform action.

nodes.label: BG 3.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Whatever a great man does, others also do; whatever he establishes as the standard, the world follows.

nodes.label: BG 3.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन
nodes.snippet: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that needs to be done by Me, nor is there anything unattained that needs to be attained; yet I engage Myself in action.

nodes.label: BG 3.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः
nodes.snippet: For, should I not ever engage myself in action, unwearied, people would in every way follow my path, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 3.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्
nodes.snippet: These worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I would be the author of confusion of castes and destruction of these beings.

nodes.label: BG 3.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: As the ignorant act out of attachment to action, O Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing for the welfare of the world.

nodes.label: BG 3.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Let no wise man unsettle the minds of ignorant people who are attached to action; he should engage them in all actions, himself fulfilling them with devotion.

nodes.label: BG 3.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: All actions are wrought in all cases by the qualities of Nature alone. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."

nodes.label: BG 3.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed Arjuna, about the divisions of the qualities and their functions, knowing that the Gunas, as senses, move amidst the Gunas, as the…

nodes.label: BG 3.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those deluded by the qualities of Nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish one who is of imperfect…

nodes.label: BG 3.30
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind centered on the Self, free from hope and egoism, and from mental fever, fight thou.

nodes.label: BG 3.31
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those who constantly practice this teaching of Mine with faith and without caviling, they too are freed from actions.

nodes.label: BG 3.32
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But those who criticize My teaching and do not practice it, deprived of all knowledge and lacking discernment, know them to be doomed to destruction.

nodes.label: BG 3.33
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Even a wise man acts in accordance with his own nature; beings will follow their nature; what can restraint do?

nodes.label: BG 3.34
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses; let no one come under their sway; for, they are his enemies.

nodes.label: BG 3.35
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear.

nodes.label: BG 3.36
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "But what compels man to commit sin, even against his wishes, O Varshneya (Krishna), as if constrained by force?"

nodes.label: BG 3.37
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "It is desire and it is anger, both of the quality of Rajas, all-devouring and all-sinful; know this as the foe here in this world."

nodes.label: BG 3.38
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, and as an embryo is surrounded by the amniotic sac, so is this enveloped by that.

nodes.label: BG 3.39
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, which is insatiable like fire.

nodes.label: BG 3.40
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these, it deludes the embodied one, veiling their wisdom.

nodes.label: BG 3.41
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, control your senses first and then kill this sinful thing, which destroys knowledge and realization.

nodes.label: BG 3.42
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: They say that the senses are superior to the body; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and He (the Self) is superior even to the intellect.

nodes.label: BG 3.43
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Thus, knowing Him who is superior to the intellect and restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to conquer.

nodes.label: BG 4.1
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; he then told it to Manu; Manu proclaimed it to Ikshvaku.

nodes.label: BG 4.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: This, handed down in regular succession by the royal sages, was known. This Yoga, however, has been lost here over time, O Parantapa (burner of the foes).

nodes.label: BG 4.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः
nodes.snippet: That same ancient yoga has been today taught to you by me, for you are my devotee and my friend; it is the supreme secret.

nodes.label: BG 4.4
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "Later was Thy birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun); how am I to understand that Thou hast taught this Yoga from the beginning?"

nodes.label: BG 4.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "Many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all, but thou knowest not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes)."

nodes.label: BG 4.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Though I am unborn and of imperishable nature, and though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own nature, I am born by my own Maya.

nodes.label: BG 4.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत
nodes.snippet: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.

nodes.label: BG 4.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age.

nodes.label: BG 4.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः
nodes.snippet: He who thus knows, in their true light, My divine birth and actions, having abandoned the body, is not born again; he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 4.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained My Being.

nodes.label: BG 4.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्
nodes.snippet: In whatever way men approach Me, even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 4.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः
nodes.snippet: Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; for success is quickly attained by men through action.

nodes.label: BG 4.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; though I am the author of it, know Me as non-doer and immutable.

nodes.label: BG 4.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा
nodes.snippet: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.

nodes.label: BG 4.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः
nodes.snippet: Having known this, the ancient seekers of freedom also performed action; therefore, do thou also perform action, as the ancients did in days of yore.

nodes.label: BG 4.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. Therefore, I shall teach you the nature of action and inaction, by knowing which you will be liberated…

nodes.label: BG 4.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः
nodes.snippet: For verily, the true nature of action enjoined by the scriptures should be known, as well as that of forbidden or unlawful action, and of inaction; the nature of action is hard…

nodes.label: BG 4.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः
nodes.snippet: He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a yogi and performer of all actions.

nodes.label: BG 4.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and selfish purposes, and whose actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge, the wise call him a sage.

nodes.label: BG 4.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything even while being engaged in activity.

nodes.label: BG 4.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Without hope, controlling the mind and the self, having abandoned all covetousness, and performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin.

nodes.label: BG 4.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Content with what comes to him without effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, he acts yet is not bound.

nodes.label: BG 4.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: To one who is devoid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is…

nodes.label: BG 4.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman indeed shall be attained by one who always…

nodes.label: BG 4.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others, who have realized the Self, offer the Self as sacrifice in the fire of Brahman alone.

nodes.label: BG 4.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as a sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as a sacrifice in the fire of…

nodes.label: BG 4.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy, or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

nodes.label: BG 4.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Others again offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as sacrifice, while ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer the study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.

nodes.label: BG 4.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely…

nodes.label: BG 4.30
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in each life-breath. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed through sacrifice.

nodes.label: BG 4.31
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then can they…

nodes.label: BG 4.32
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे
nodes.snippet: Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman at the face of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action, and thus knowing, you shall be liberated.

nodes.label: BG 4.33
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacrifice with objects, O Parantapa (scorcher of the foes). All actions in their entirety, O Arjuna, culminate in knowledge.

nodes.label: BG 4.34
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Know that the wise who have realized the truth will instruct thee in that knowledge through long prostration, supplication, and service.

nodes.label: BG 4.35
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Knowing that thou shalt not, O Arjuna, again be deluded like this; and by that thou shalt see all beings in thyself and also in me.

nodes.label: BG 4.36
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet thou shalt surely cross over all sins by the raft of knowledge.

nodes.label: BG 4.37
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ash.

nodes.label: BG 4.38
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते
nodes.snippet: Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it within the Self in due time.

nodes.label: BG 4.39
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The one who is full of faith, devoted to it, and has subdued their senses obtains this knowledge; and upon obtaining the knowledge, they attain the supreme peace immediately.

nodes.label: BG 4.40
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self go to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting one.

nodes.label: BG 4.41
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who has renounced actions through Yoga, whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge, and who is self-possessed—such a one is not bound by actions, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 4.42
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge (of the Self), cut asunder the doubt of the self, born of ignorance, residing in your heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna!

nodes.label: BG 5.1
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga. Please tell me conclusively which is better of the two."

nodes.label: BG 5.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action."

nodes.label: BG 5.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति
nodes.snippet: He should be known as a perpetual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily freed from bondage.

nodes.label: BG 5.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action, or the performance of action, as though they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one,…

nodes.label: BG 5.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is also reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one,…

nodes.label: BG 5.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But, O mighty-armed Arjuna, renunciation is hard to attain without Yoga; the sage who is in harmony with Yoga quickly goes to Brahman.

nodes.label: BG 5.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is pure, who has conquered the self, who has subdued his senses, and who realizes his Self as the Self in all beings, though…

nodes.label: BG 5.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonized knower of Truth think, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing.

nodes.label: BG 5.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening, and closing the eyes, one should be convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.

nodes.label: BG 5.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः
nodes.snippet: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not tainted by water.

nodes.label: BG 5.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only through the body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, for the purification of the self.

nodes.label: BG 5.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The one who is united (the well-poised or harmonized) having abandoned the fruit of action attains eternal peace; whereas the one who is not united (the unsteady or…

nodes.label: BG 5.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Mentally renouncing all actions and being self-controlled, the embodied one happily rests in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing others (body and senses) to act.

nodes.label: BG 5.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः
nodes.snippet: Neither does the Lord create agency nor actions for the world, nor union with the fruits of actions; rather, it is Nature that acts.

nodes.label: BG 5.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः
nodes.snippet: The Lord takes neither the demerit nor the merit of any; knowledge is enveloped by ignorance, and beings are deluded.

nodes.label: BG 5.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But to those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, like the sun, knowledge reveals the Supreme Brahman.

nodes.label: BG 5.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Their intellect absorbed in That, their self being That, established in That, with That as their supreme goal, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by knowledge.

nodes.label: BG 5.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Sages look with an equal eye on a Brahmana endowed with learning and humility, on a cow, an elephant, a dog, and even an outcaste.

nodes.label: BG 5.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः
nodes.snippet: Even here in this world, those whose minds rest in reality overcome birth; Brahman is indeed spotless and real; therefore they are established in Brahman.

nodes.label: BG 5.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Resting in Brahman, with a steady intellect and undeluded, the knower of Brahman neither rejoices upon obtaining what is pleasant nor grieves upon obtaining what is unpleasant.

nodes.label: BG 5.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: With the self unattached to external contacts, he finds happiness in the Self; with the self engaged in the meditation of Brahman, he attains endless happiness.

nodes.label: BG 5.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते
nodes.snippet: The enjoyments that arise from contact are only sources of pain, for they have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna; the wise do not rejoice in them.

nodes.label: BG 5.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who is able, while still here in this world, to withstand the impulse born out of desire and anger before the liberation from the body, he is a Yogi, and he is a happy man.

nodes.label: BG 5.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who is happy within, who rejoices within, and who is illuminated within, that Yogi attains absolute freedom, or Moksha, becoming Brahman himself.

nodes.label: BG 5.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The sages obtain absolute freedom or Moksha when their sins have been destroyed, their dualities have been torn asunder, they are self-controlled, and they are intent on the…

nodes.label: BG 5.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Absolute freedom exists on all sides for those self-controlled ascetics who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled their thoughts, and who have realized the Self.

nodes.label: BG 5.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Shutting out all external contacts and fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, realizing the outgoing and incoming breaths moving within the nostrils.

nodes.label: BG 5.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: With the senses, mind, and intellect ever controlled, having liberation as their supreme goal, free from desire, fear, and anger, the sage is truly liberated forever.

nodes.label: BG 5.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who knows Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, attains peace.

nodes.label: BG 6.1
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions—he is a sannyasi and a yogi, not he who is without fire and without action.

nodes.label: BG 6.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव
nodes.snippet: Do you, O Arjuna, know that Yoga is what they call renunciation; no one indeed becomes a Yogi who has not renounced their thoughts.

nodes.label: BG 6.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained Yoga, inaction is said to be the means.

nodes.label: BG 6.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When a person is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then they are said to have attained Yoga.

nodes.label: BG 6.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: One should raise oneself by one's own self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the self alone is one's own friend, and the self alone is one's own enemy.

nodes.label: BG 6.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Self is the friend of the self of him by whom the Self has been conquered; but to the unconquered self, this Self stands in the position of an enemy, like an external foe.

nodes.label: BG 6.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Supreme Self of him who is self-controlled and peaceful remains balanced in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor.

nodes.label: BG 6.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Yogi who is satisfied with the knowledge and wisdom of the Self, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and gold are all the same, is…

nodes.label: BG 6.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who is of the same mind towards the good-hearted, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relatives, the righteous, and the unrighteous, excels.

nodes.label: BG 6.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Let the yogi constantly strive to keep the mind steady, remaining in solitude, alone, with the body and mind controlled, and free from hope and greed.

nodes.label: BG 6.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of cloth, skin, and kusha grass layered one over the other.

nodes.label: BG 6.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practice Yoga for the purification of the self.

nodes.label: BG 6.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Let him firmly hold his body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose without looking around.

nodes.label: BG 6.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled their mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let them sit, having Me as their supreme goal.

nodes.label: BG 6.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Thus, always keeping the mind balanced, the yogi, with the mind controlled, attains the peace abiding in Me, culminating in liberation.

nodes.label: BG 6.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Verily, Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is always awake, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 6.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such as walking, etc.), who exercises moderation in action, and who is moderate in sleep…

nodes.label: BG 6.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any of the objects of desire, then it is said, 'He is united'.

nodes.label: BG 6.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता
nodes.snippet: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker, so is the Yogi of a controlled mind, who practices Yoga in the Self, compared.

nodes.label: BG 6.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, attains quietude, and when one sees the Self by the Self, they are satisfied in their own Self.

nodes.label: BG 6.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: When he (the Yogi) feels that infinite bliss which can be grasped by the pure intellect and which transcends the senses, and is established therein, never moving away from the…

nodes.label: BG 6.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः
nodes.snippet: Having obtained it, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; established in it, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.

nodes.label: BG 6.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Let this be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undespairing mind.

nodes.label: BG 6.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Abandoning unreservedly all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of senses by the mind from all sides.

nodes.label: BG 6.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Little by little, let him attain steadiness of the intellect by holding it firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything else.

nodes.label: BG 6.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it from that and bring it under the control of the Self alone.

nodes.label: BG 6.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Supreme Bliss indeed comes to this Yogi whose mind is made peaceful, whose passion is quelled, who has become Brahman, and who is free from sin.

nodes.label: BG 6.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of yoga), is freed from sins and easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).

nodes.label: BG 6.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: With the mind harmonized by Yoga, he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.

nodes.label: BG 6.30
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति
nodes.snippet: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, never becomes separated from Me, nor do I from him.

nodes.label: BG 6.31
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who, being established in unity, worships Me, who dwells in all beings, that yogi abides in Me, whatever their mode of living may be.

nodes.label: BG 6.32
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees reality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, is regarded as the highest Yogi.

nodes.label: BG 6.33
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, I do not see how this Yoga of equanimity, which you have taught me, can be maintained steadily, due to the restlessness of the mind."

nodes.label: BG 6.34
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्
nodes.snippet: The mind is indeed restless, turbulent, strong, and unyielding, O Krishna; I consider it as difficult to control as controlling the wind.

nodes.label: BG 6.35
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but with practice and dispassion, it can be restrained."

nodes.label: BG 6.36
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः
nodes.snippet: I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one with an uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain it by the appropriate means.

nodes.label: BG 6.37
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "He who is unable to control himself, even though he has faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he meet, having failed to attain perfection in…

nodes.label: BG 6.38
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a rent cloud, supportless, O mighty-armed one, deluded on the path of Brahman?

nodes.label: BG 6.39
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: O Krishna, please completely dispel this doubt of mine, for it is not possible for anyone but You to do so.

nodes.label: BG 6.40
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the next will there be destruction for him; none, indeed, who does good, O my son, ever comes to grief."

nodes.label: BG 6.41
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is born in a house of the pure and wealthy.

nodes.label: BG 6.42
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Or he is born in a family of even the wisest of yogis; verily, such a birth is very difficult to obtain in this world.

nodes.label: BG 6.43
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Then he comes into contact with the knowledge acquired in his former body and strives even more for perfection, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 6.44
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: By that same former practice, he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmanic word.

nodes.label: BG 6.45
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But the Yogi who strives assiduously, purified of sins and perfected gradually over many births, reaches the highest goal.

nodes.label: BG 6.46
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics, even superior to those who have knowledge obtained through the study of scriptures; he is also superior to men of action;…

nodes.label: BG 6.47
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: And among all the Yogis, he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devoted.

nodes.label: BG 7.1
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, hear how you shall, without doubt, know Me fully, with your mind intent on Me, practicing Yoga and taking refuge in Me."

nodes.label: BG 7.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: I will declare to you in full this knowledge combined with realization, after knowing which nothing else remains to be known here.

nodes.label: BG 7.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Among thousands of men, one may perchance strive for perfection; even among those successful strivers, only one may perchance know Me in essence.

nodes.label: BG 7.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च
nodes.snippet: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and egoism—thus is My Nature divided eightfold.

nodes.label: BG 7.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: O mighty-armed Arjuna, this is the inferior Prakriti; know it as distinct from My higher Prakriti, the very life-element, by which this world is upheld.

nodes.label: BG 7.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Know that these two are the womb of all beings; thus, I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.

nodes.label: BG 7.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: There is nothing higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, like clusters of gems on a string.

nodes.label: BG 7.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: I am the flavor in water, O Arjuna; I am the light in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in the ether and virility in men.

nodes.label: BG 7.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ
nodes.snippet: I am the sweet fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in the fire, the life in all beings, and I am the austerity of ascetics.

nodes.label: BG 7.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्
nodes.snippet: Know Me, O Arjuna, as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intelligence of the intelligent, and the splendour of the splendid objects.

nodes.label: BG 7.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Of the strong, I am the strength devoid of desire and attachment, and in all beings, I am the desire in accordance with Dharma, O Arjuna.

nodes.label: BG 7.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये
nodes.snippet: Whatever beings (and objects) that are pure, active, and inert, know that they proceed from Me. They are in Me, yet I am not in them.

nodes.label: BG 7.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Deluded by these Natures, composed of the three qualities of Nature, all this world does not know Me as distinct from them and immutable.

nodes.label: BG 7.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया
nodes.snippet: Verily, this divine illusion of Mine, composed of the three qualities, is difficult to cross over; those who take refuge in Me alone, can cross over this illusion.

nodes.label: BG 7.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः
nodes.snippet: The evil-doers and the deluded, who are the lowest of men, do not seek Me; those whose knowledge is destroyed by illusion follow the ways of demons.

nodes.label: BG 7.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna, and they are the distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the wise, O Lord of the Bharatas.

nodes.label: BG 7.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Of them, the wise who are ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excel; for I am exceedingly dear to the wise, and they are dear to Me.

nodes.label: BG 7.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्
nodes.snippet: Indeed, all these are noble; however, I consider the wise man as My very Self; for, he is steadfast in mind and established in Me alone as the supreme goal.

nodes.label: BG 7.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: At the end of many births, the wise man comes to Me, realizing that all this is Vaasudeva (the innermost Self); such a great soul (Mahatma) is very hard to find.

nodes.label: BG 7.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those whose wisdom has been taken away by this or that desire, go to other gods, following this or that rite, led by their own nature.

nodes.label: BG 7.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति
nodes.snippet: Whatever form any devotee desires to worship with faith, I make that same faith of his firm and unflinching.

nodes.label: BG 7.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that form and obtains his desired outcome, which is ordained by Me alone.

nodes.label: BG 7.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Verily, the reward (fruit) that accrues to those men of small intelligence is finite. The worshippers of the gods go to them, whereas My devotees come to Me.

nodes.label: BG 7.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The foolish think of Me, the Unmanifest, as having manifestation, not knowing My higher, immutable, and most excellent nature.

nodes.label: BG 7.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: I am not manifest to all, veiled as I am by the Yoga-Maya. This deluded world does not know Me, who am unborn and imperishable.

nodes.label: BG 7.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: I know, O Arjuna, the beings of the past, the present, and the future; however, no one knows Me.

nodes.label: BG 7.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: O Bharata, all beings are subject to delusion at birth due to the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O Parantapa.

nodes.label: BG 7.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But those men of virtuous deeds, whose sins have come to an end and who are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me steadfastly, with their vows.

nodes.label: BG 7.29
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me, realize in full that Brahman, the whole knowledge of the Self, and all action.

nodes.label: BG 7.30
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः
nodes.snippet: Those who know Me with the Adhibhuta (pertaining to the elements), Adhidaiva (pertaining to the gods), and the Adhiyajna (pertaining to the sacrifice) know Me even at the time…

nodes.label: BG 8.1
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.sa: किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम
nodes.snippet: Arjuna said, "What is Brahman? What is Adhyatma? What is action, O best among men? What is Adhibhuta declared to be? And, what is Adhidaiva said to be?"

nodes.label: BG 8.2
nodes.speaker: arjuna
nodes.snippet: Who and how is Adhiyajna here in this body, O destroyer of Madhu? And how, at the time of death, are You to be known by the self-controlled?

nodes.label: BG 8.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "Brahman is the Imperishable, the Supreme; its essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the offering (to the gods) that causes the existence and…

nodes.label: BG 8.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Adhibhuta—knowledge of the elements—pertains to My perishable nature, and the Purusha, or the Soul, is the Adhidaiva; I alone am the Adhiyajna here in this body, O best among…

nodes.label: BG 8.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: And whoever, leaving their body, goes forth remembering Me alone at the time of death, they will attain My Being; there is no doubt about this.

nodes.label: BG 8.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्
nodes.snippet: Whoever at the end leaves the body, thinking of any being, to that being only does he go, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), due to his constant thought of that being.

nodes.label: BG 8.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Therefore, at all times, remember Me only and fight. With your mind and intellect fixed on Me, you will undoubtedly come to Me alone.

nodes.label: BG 8.8
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: With the mind not moving towards any other thing, made steadfast through the practice of habitual meditation, and constantly meditating, one goes to the Supreme Person, the…

nodes.label: BG 8.9
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Whosoever meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler of the whole world, minuter than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun and…

nodes.label: BG 8.10
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: At the time of death, with an unwavering mind, endowed with devotion, by the power of Yoga, fixing the whole life-breath in the middle of the two eyebrows, he reaches that…

nodes.label: BG 8.11
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: That which is declared to be Imperishable by those who know the Vedas, that which the self-controlled (ascetics or Sannyasins) and passion-free enter, that goal, desiring which…

nodes.label: BG 8.12
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च
nodes.snippet: Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart, and fixed the life-breath in the head, engage in the practice of concentration.

nodes.label: BG 8.13
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Uttering the one-syllabled Om, the Brahman, and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains the Supreme Goal.

nodes.label: BG 8.14
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः
nodes.snippet: I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast yogi who constantly and daily remembers me for a long time, not thinking of anything else with a single-minded or one-pointed…

nodes.label: BG 8.15
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Having attained Me, these great souls do not take birth again here—a place of pain and impermanence—but have reached the highest perfection of liberation.

nodes.label: BG 8.16
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: All the worlds, including the world of Brahma, are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rebirth.

nodes.label: BG 8.17
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those who know the day of Brahma, which lasts a thousand Yugas, and the night, which also lasts a thousand Yugas, know day and night.

nodes.label: BG 8.18
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: From the Unmanifested, all the manifested worlds proceed upon the arrival of the 'day'; upon the arrival of the 'night', they dissolve indeed into that which is known as the…

nodes.label: BG 8.19
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते
nodes.snippet: This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, helplessly dissolves, O Arjuna, into the Unmanifested at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the…

nodes.label: BG 8.20
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: But verily, there exists higher than this Unmanifested, another Unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed even when all beings are destroyed.

nodes.label: BG 8.21
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: What is known as the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That is said to be the highest goal. Those who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My supreme abode (place…

nodes.label: BG 8.22
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया
nodes.snippet: That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone, within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.

nodes.label: BG 8.23
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Now I will tell you, O chief of the Bharatas, the times of departure at which the Yogis will return or not return.

nodes.label: BG 8.24
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice) departing, then men who know Brahman go to Brahman.

nodes.label: BG 8.25
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Attaining the lunar light through smoke, night time, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the yogi returns.

nodes.label: BG 8.26
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते
nodes.snippet: The bright and dark paths of the world are thought to be eternal; one leads to no return, and the other leads to return.

nodes.label: BG 8.27
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन
nodes.snippet: Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no yogi is deluded; therefore, at all times, be steadfast in yoga.

nodes.label: BG 8.28
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts,…

nodes.label: BG 9.1
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: The Blessed Lord said, "I shall now declare to thee, who does not cavil, the greatest secret—the knowledge combined with experience (Self-realisation). Having known this, thou…

nodes.label: BG 9.2
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: This is the royal science, the royal secret, the supreme purifier, realizable by direct intuitive knowledge, according to righteousness, very easy to perform and imperishable.

nodes.label: BG 9.3
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: Those who have no faith in this Dharma, O Parantapa, return to the path of this world without attaining Me.

nodes.label: BG 9.4
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: All of this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest aspect; all beings exist within Me, but I do not dwell within them.

nodes.label: BG 9.5
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.sa: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्
nodes.snippet: Nor do beings exist in Me (in reality); behold, My divine Yoga, which supports all beings, but does not dwell in them, is My Self, the efficient cause of beings.

nodes.label: BG 9.6
nodes.speaker: krishna
nodes.snippet: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always rests in the ether, so too, know that all beings rest in Me.

nodes.label: BG 9.7
nodes.speaker: krishna
