nodes.desc: Union through selfless, skilful action offered to the Divine — 'yoga is skill in action' (2.50). Krishna's answer to Arjuna's wish to escape the battlefield.

nodes.label: Tyāga
nodes.desc: Relinquishing the fruit of action while still acting — distinguished from saṃnyāsa (giving up action) in 18.2, and declared the true renunciation (18.11).

nodes.label: Saṃnyāsa
nodes.desc: Formal renunciation of action. The Gita reinterprets it inwardly: the true saṃnyāsī neither hates nor desires (5.3) and performs duty without depending on its fruit (6.1).

nodes.label: Yajña
nodes.desc: Action as offering. 'Work done as yajña does not bind' (3.9); Chapter 4 widens yajña to knowledge, breath, study and self-restraint, culminating in 'brahmārpaṇam' (4.24).

nodes.label: Dāna
nodes.desc: Giving — sattvic when given as duty, at the right place and time, to a worthy recipient, expecting nothing in return (17.20).

nodes.label: Tapas
nodes.desc: Disciplined heat of effort — austerity of body, speech and mind (17.14–16), sattvic when undertaken with faith and without desire for reward.

nodes.label: Jñāna
nodes.desc: Direct, liberating knowledge of reality. 'There is no purifier in this world like knowledge' (4.38); its marks are humility, non-violence, patience and the rest (13.8–12).

nodes.label: Vijñāna
nodes.desc: Knowledge made experiential — jñāna together with vijñāna, 'knowing which nothing more remains to be known' (7.2, 9.1).

nodes.label: Ajñāna
nodes.desc: The veil over knowledge that deludes beings (5.15). 'The ignorant, the faithless and the doubting soul perish' (4.40).

nodes.label: Jñānayoga
nodes.desc: The contemplative path of discrimination between the Self and not-Self — one of the 'two paths' Krishna described of old (3.3).

nodes.label: Sāṃkhya
nodes.desc: The analytical understanding of Self and matter that Krishna teaches first (2.11–30) before turning to the yoga of action (2.39).

nodes.label: Sthitaprajña
nodes.desc: The person whose wisdom is established — content in the Self, unshaken by sorrow, free of craving, fear and anger. Portrayed in eighteen verses (2.55–72) answering Arjuna's question (2.54).

nodes.label: Guṇātīta
nodes.desc: One who has gone beyond sattva, rajas and tamas — the same in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, honour and dishonour (14.22–26).

nodes.label: Kṣetra-kṣetrajña
nodes.desc: The body-mind is the 'field'; the conscious witness who knows it is the 'knower of the field' (13.2–3) — the analytical heart of Chapter 13.

nodes.label: Bhakti
nodes.desc: Loving devotion to the Divine. 'Whoever offers me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water — that I accept' (9.26); the beloved devotee is described in 12.13–20.

nodes.label: Bhaktiyoga
nodes.desc: Union through unwavering love — the theme of Chapter 12, where Krishna names those 'ever-united, endowed with supreme faith' as the most perfect in yoga (12.2).

nodes.label: Ananya bhakti
nodes.desc: Devotion with no other refuge. 'To those who worship me with undivided minds, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have' (9.22).

nodes.label: Śaraṇāgati
nodes.desc: Taking refuge in the Divine. Arjuna begins as a disciple who has 'surrendered' (2.7); Krishna's final word is 'abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone' (18.66).

nodes.label: Anugraha
nodes.desc: The Divine's compassionate grace that dispels darkness from within (10.11) and by which the devotee attains the eternal abode (18.56).

nodes.label: Smaraṇa
nodes.desc: Constant remembrance, especially at life's end: 'whatever state one remembers on leaving the body, to that one goes' (8.6). 'Remember me and fight' (8.7).

nodes.label: Oṃ
nodes.desc: The one-syllabled Brahman (8.13), 'praṇava in all the Vedas' (7.8) — and the opening of 'oṃ tat sat', the threefold designation of the Absolute (17.23).

nodes.label: Yoga
nodes.desc: Defined three ways: 'evenness of mind is yoga' (2.48), 'yoga is skill in action' (2.50), and 'the severance of union with sorrow' (6.23).

nodes.label: Dhyāna
nodes.desc: Meditative absorption. Chapter 6 gives the method — a clean seat, steady posture, gaze fixed, mind on the Self — 'like a lamp in a windless place' (6.19).

nodes.label: Abhyāsa
nodes.desc: Repeated, patient effort. With vairāgya it is Krishna's answer to the restless mind: 'it is restrained by practice and dispassion' (6.35).

nodes.label: Vairāgya
nodes.desc: Freedom from the colouring of desire — the twin of abhyāsa (6.35) and the 'firm sword of detachment' that fells the aśvattha tree of saṃsāra (15.3).

nodes.label: Indriyanigraha
nodes.desc: Withdrawing the senses from their objects 'as the tortoise withdraws its limbs' (2.58). The senses are powerful, but the self-controlled attain peace (2.61, 2.64).

nodes.label: Yuktāhāravihāra
nodes.desc: 'Yoga is not for one who eats too much or too little, sleeps too much or too little' — moderation in food, recreation, work and rest makes yoga the destroyer of sorrow (6.16–17).

nodes.label: Prāṇa
nodes.desc: The life-breath offered in prāṇāyāma (4.29), balanced between the nostrils in meditation (5.27) and drawn between the brows at the moment of death (8.10).

nodes.label: Samatva
nodes.desc: Sameness of mind in success and failure, pleasure and pain, friend and foe. 'Evenness of mind is called yoga' (2.48).

nodes.label: Śraddhātraya
nodes.desc: Faith shaped by one's guṇas — 'a person is made of faith; as one's faith is, so is one' (17.3). Chapter 17 classifies worship, food, sacrifice, austerity and charity by sattva, rajas and tamas.

nodes.label: Ātman
nodes.desc: The undying Self: 'It is not born, nor does it ever die… unborn, eternal, ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain' (2.20). Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it (2.23).

nodes.label: Brahman
nodes.desc: The imperishable supreme reality (8.3) — 'beginningless, neither being nor non-being' (13.13). Offering, oblation and fire are all Brahman (4.24).

nodes.label: Paramātman
nodes.desc: The supreme Self seated in the body as witness, permitter, supporter and enjoyer (13.23), indwelling all beings 'in the region of the heart' (18.61).

nodes.label: Puruṣottama
nodes.desc: Beyond the perishable and even the imperishable is the Supreme Person, celebrated in the world and the Veda as Puruṣottama (15.16–18).

nodes.label: Īśvara
nodes.desc: The Lord who dwells in the hearts of all beings, turning them as if mounted on a machine by māyā (18.61).

nodes.label: Avatāra
nodes.desc: 'Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, I manifest myself… to protect the good, destroy evil and re-establish dharma, I come into being age after age' (4.7–8).

nodes.label: Māyā
nodes.desc: The Lord's power composed of the guṇas, 'hard to cross'; only those who take refuge in him pass beyond it (7.14).

nodes.label: Prakṛti
nodes.desc: Nature, eightfold in its lower form (7.4) and the source of all transformations and guṇas (13.20). 'All actions are performed by the guṇas of prakṛti' (3.27).

nodes.label: Puruṣa
nodes.desc: The conscious principle that, seated in prakṛti, experiences the guṇas (13.22) — beginningless, like prakṛti itself (13.20).

nodes.label: Akṣara
nodes.desc: That which does not decay — the supreme Brahman (8.3), the unmanifest beyond the unmanifest, 'the highest goal' (8.21).

nodes.label: Adhyātma
nodes.desc: One's own essential nature — named in Krishna's reply to Arjuna's seven questions at the opening of Chapter 8 (8.3).

nodes.label: Viśvarūpa
nodes.desc: The universal form revealed to Arjuna with divine sight (11.8) — 'as if a thousand suns blazed forth at once' (11.12), and as Time the world-destroyer (11.32).

nodes.label: Vibhūti
nodes.desc: The glories of the Divine in the world: 'whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that to spring from a spark of my splendour' (10.41).

nodes.label: Kāla
nodes.desc: 'I am Time, the mighty destroyer of the worlds' (11.32) — and among measurers, Krishna is time itself (10.30, 10.33).

nodes.label: Triguṇa
nodes.desc: Sattva, rajas and tamas — the three strands of nature that bind the embodied Self (14.5). 'Be free of the three guṇas, O Arjuna' (2.45).

nodes.label: Sattva
nodes.desc: The guṇa of light, health and knowledge; it binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge (14.6).

nodes.label: Rajas
nodes.desc: The guṇa of passion, born of craving and attachment; it binds through attachment to action (14.7). Kāma and krodha are 'born of rajas' (3.37).

nodes.label: Tamas
nodes.desc: The guṇa of inertia born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds through heedlessness, indolence and sleep (14.8).

nodes.label: Saṃsāra
nodes.desc: The ocean of death-bound existence from which Krishna 'swiftly lifts' those whose minds are fixed on him (12.7); the inverted aśvattha tree of Chapter 15.

nodes.label: Punarjanma
nodes.desc: 'As a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters new ones' (2.22).

nodes.label: Mokṣa
nodes.desc: Release from bondage and rebirth. 'I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve' (18.66).

nodes.label: Nirvāṇa
nodes.desc: Brahma-nirvāṇa — the peace of the Absolute attained by the one free from desire (2.72), self-delighted and illumined within (5.24–26).

nodes.label: Veda
nodes.desc: Revealed scripture — honoured, yet relativised: for the knower of Brahman the Vedas are 'like a pond when there is a flood everywhere' (2.46). 'I am that which is to be known by all the Vedas' (15.15).

nodes.label: Manas
nodes.desc: The mind — 'restless, turbulent, powerful and obstinate', as hard to control as the wind (6.34), yet the Self's best friend once conquered (6.6).

nodes.label: Buddhi
nodes.desc: The faculty of discernment. A resolute buddhi is single-pointed (2.41); its sattvic form knows what is to be done and what not (18.30).

nodes.label: Svabhāva
nodes.desc: Each being's innate nature, from which its duties arise. 'Beings follow their nature — what can repression accomplish?' (3.33).

nodes.label: Viṣāda
nodes.desc: The collapse of will that gives Chapter 1 its name — Arjuna sinks down in his chariot, bow slipping from his hand (1.47).

nodes.label: Śoka
nodes.desc: Sorrow over loss. Krishna's first words: 'You grieve for those who should not be grieved for… the wise grieve neither for the living nor the dead' (2.11).

nodes.label: Moha
nodes.desc: Clouded understanding about what is right. Arjuna's 'mind is confused about dharma' (2.7); his last words are 'my delusion is destroyed' (18.73).

nodes.label: Bhaya
nodes.desc: Fear for oneself and one's world. Even Arjuna, beholding the cosmic form, confesses 'my mind is shaken with fear' (11.45).

nodes.label: Cintā
nodes.desc: Endless anxious calculation about results — the 'immeasurable worry, ending only at death' of those driven by desire (16.11).

nodes.label: Krodha
nodes.desc: Desire thwarted becomes anger; 'from anger comes delusion' (2.63). Anger is one of the three gates to self-ruin (16.21).

nodes.label: Kāma
nodes.desc: Insatiable desire, 'the great devourer, the enemy here' (3.37) that veils wisdom like smoke veils fire (3.38).

nodes.label: Lobha
nodes.desc: Grasping for more. Arjuna sees the Kauravas' 'minds overpowered by greed' (1.38); greed is the third gate of ruin (16.21).

nodes.label: Ahaṅkāra
nodes.desc: The 'I-maker' that claims doership: 'deluded by ego, one thinks I am the doer' (3.27).

nodes.label: Dambha
nodes.desc: 'Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance' mark the demonic endowment (16.4).

nodes.label: Dveṣa
nodes.desc: Recoil and hatred — the twin of attachment (3.34). The beloved devotee is 'without hatred for any being' (12.13).

nodes.label: Saṅga
nodes.desc: Clinging to people, things and outcomes. 'Brooding on objects, attachment is born' (2.62) — the first link of the cascade.

nodes.label: Viṣaya-dhyāna
nodes.desc: Dwelling on objects of the senses — the seed of the 2.62 cascade: 'when a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born'.

nodes.label: Sammoha
nodes.desc: 'From anger arises bewilderment' (2.63) — the clouding that follows rage.

nodes.label: Smṛti-vibhrama
nodes.desc: 'From bewilderment, confusion of memory' (2.63) — one forgets what one knows and who one is; restored in 18.73 ('smṛtir labdhā').

nodes.label: Buddhi-nāśa
nodes.desc: 'From confusion of memory, the loss of reason' (2.63) — the discriminating intellect itself is destroyed.

nodes.label: Praṇāśa
nodes.desc: 'From the loss of reason, one perishes' (2.63). Desire, anger and greed are 'the threefold gate of hell, destructive of the self' (16.21).
nodes.modern: Downward spiral, burnout of the self

nodes.label: Saṃśaya
nodes.desc: Corrosive doubt: 'for the doubting soul there is neither this world nor the next, nor happiness' (4.40).

nodes.label: Klaibya
nodes.desc: 'Yield not to unmanliness… cast off this petty weakness of heart and arise' (2.3) — Krishna's first rousing call.

nodes.label: Cāñcalya
nodes.desc: 'The mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate; I think it as hard to control as the wind' (6.34).

nodes.label: Pramāda
nodes.desc: Heedlessness, indolence and sleep — the binding marks of tamas (14.8), whose happiness 'deludes the self from beginning to end' (18.39).

nodes.label: Duḥkha
nodes.desc: Pain in all its forms. Yoga is 'the severance of union with sorrow' (6.23); pleasures born of contact are 'wombs of sorrow' (5.22).

nodes.label: Śānti
nodes.desc: Peace that comes not from fulfilling desires but from their quieting: 'as rivers enter the full ocean… that person attains peace' (2.70).

nodes.label: Abhaya
nodes.desc: First of the divine endowments (16.1). Krishna's closing assurance 'do not grieve' (18.66) is the seal of fearlessness.

nodes.label: Śraddhā
nodes.desc: 'The one with faith attains knowledge… and soon attains supreme peace' (4.39). A person is 'made of faith' (17.3).

nodes.label: Karuṇā
nodes.desc: Friendliness and compassion for all beings (12.13), mercy (16.2). Distinct from Arjuna's sentimental pity (kṛpā, 1.28; 2.1), which Krishna does not endorse.

nodes.label: Santoṣa
nodes.desc: 'When one is satisfied in the Self by the Self alone' (2.55); 'content with whatever comes unbidden' (4.22); 'ever content' (12.14).

nodes.label: Prasāda
nodes.desc: Clear tranquillity of mind: 'in serenity all sorrows come to an end, and the intellect of the serene soon becomes steady' (2.65).

nodes.label: Dhṛti
nodes.desc: Steadfastness that holds mind, breath and senses on course (18.33); the sattvic doer is 'endowed with fortitude and enthusiasm' (18.26).

nodes.label: Sukha
nodes.desc: Sattvic happiness is 'like poison at first but nectar in the end' (18.37); the yogi touches 'boundless bliss' (6.21, 6.28).

nodes.label: Kṣamā
nodes.desc: Forbearance — named among Krishna's own glories (10.34), the divine endowments (16.3) and the marks of the beloved devotee ('kṣamī', 12.13).

nodes.label: Maitrī
nodes.desc: Goodwill toward all: Krishna is 'the friend of all beings' (5.29); the devotee is 'friendly and compassionate' (12.13).

nodes.label: Utsāha
nodes.desc: Energetic zeal free of ego — the sattvic doer is 'endowed with fortitude and enthusiasm, unmoved by success or failure' (18.26).

nodes.label: Duty vs. Personal Attachment
nodes.desc: When what is right collides with the people you love — Arjuna's own crisis on the battlefield.

nodes.label: Fear of Failure & Outcome Anxiety
nodes.desc: Paralysis from fixating on results — exams, careers, launches, verdicts.

nodes.label: Burnout & Exhaustion
nodes.desc: Running on empty — overwork, depletion, the loss of meaning in effort.

nodes.label: Loss & Bereavement
nodes.desc: The death of someone dear — and the question of what, if anything, survives.

nodes.label: Imposter Syndrome & Self-Doubt
nodes.desc: Feeling inadequate, a fraud, unworthy of one's role — the voice that says 'not me'.

nodes.label: Dealing with Toxic or Unjust People
nodes.desc: Living or working with those who harm, manipulate or wrong you.

nodes.label: Mastering a Restless Mind
nodes.desc: Distraction, racing thoughts and the struggle to focus or meditate.

nodes.label: Moral Ambiguity in Leadership
nodes.desc: Hard calls with no clean option, when others look to you for the example.

nodes.label: Finding Life Purpose (Svadharma)
nodes.desc: What am I meant to do? The search for vocation, calling and alignment.
keywords: what should i do with my life

nodes.label: Anger & Reactivity
nodes.desc: Rage, irritability, saying and doing what you later regret.

nodes.label: Addiction, Cravings & Compulsive Habits
nodes.desc: Substances, screens, food, gambling — the pull that overrides intention.

nodes.label: Comparison, Envy & Social Status
nodes.desc: Measuring your life against others' — and the restlessness it breeds.

nodes.label: Guilt, Shame & Self-Blame
nodes.desc: Carrying past wrongs — and wondering whether redemption is possible.

nodes.label: Fear of Death & Mortality
nodes.desc: Anxiety about dying, illness, ageing — one's own or a loved one's.

nodes.label: Loneliness & Feeling Abandoned
nodes.desc: Isolation, abandonment, the sense that no one is with you.

nodes.label: Decision Paralysis & Confusion
nodes.desc: Stuck between options; afraid to choose wrong; asking others to decide.

nodes.label: Pride & Ego after Success
nodes.desc: When achievement inflates the sense of 'I did this' — and isolates.

nodes.label: Pleasure vs. Long-term Good
nodes.desc: Choosing what feels good now over what is good in the end.

nodes.label: Work-Life Balance
nodes.desc: Overcommitment, neglect of body and relationships, or the opposite — avoidance.

nodes.label: Coping with Criticism & Praise
nodes.desc: Being shaken by feedback, reviews, public opinion — or needing applause.

nodes.label: Spiritual Doubt & Crisis of Faith
nodes.desc: Losing faith, wondering if the path is real, if effort counts, if anyone listens.

nodes.label: Starting Over after Setbacks
nodes.desc: Failed attempts, relapses, broken streaks — and the courage to begin again.
